title: Dataverse: build solutions with coding agents using the Dataverse plugin and Work IQ
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, controls, permissions and consumption billing are supported. Minor corrections should remove obsolete preview labels from reference titles and acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance about Work IQ defaults.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Dataverse plugin preview pages publish no plugin-specific price as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse plugin AI agents licensing charges price Copilot; Dataverse plugin coding agents enable disable admin switch licensing price. Opened agents-plugin/, coding-agents and security-governance; prerequisites name plans, but these pages give no plugin-specific price.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Preview use does not remove underlying service charges.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP search_data uses usage-based Copilot Credit billing.
claims.quote: The search_data tool uses usage-based Copilot Credit billing rather than a fixed charge per tool call.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP search_data consumption is attributed to the calling service.
claims.quote: Consumption is attributed to the calling service and calculated according to its applicable usage-based rate card.

claims.claim: All other Dataverse MCP tools, including metadata search, use the basic text and generative AI tools Copilot Credit rate per 10 responses.
claims.quote: All other tools, including the metadata search tool, follow the text and generative AI tools (basic) Copilot Credit rate per 10 responses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Direct Work IQ API use is paid through usage-based Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Coding-agent and custom-integration calls directly to Work IQ are reported under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The coding agent's own subscription or consumption charges are separate.

claims.quote: Other tools used by the plugin, such as the Dataverse SDK for Python and Power Platform CLI, authenticate directly and aren't subject to these MCP-specific controls.

claims.quote: Their requests still require Dataverse authorization.

claims.claim: Business skills require Work IQ enabled in the environment.
claims.quote: To enable business skills in a Dataverse environment, a Power Platform administrator turns on Work IQ.

claims.claim: The Work IQ default-settings article says Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants.
claims.fix: After the default-enablement paragraph, add: 'Microsoft's general Manage feature settings article still lists the default for "Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences" as Off, unlike the new-production-environment default in the Work IQ article.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/settings-features#dataverse-intelligence-preview.

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to Work IQ default enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to Work IQ default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to Work IQ default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: The previously documented November 2026 Work IQ default-enablement schedule for existing environments has been deferred.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.claim: The Work IQ default-settings article states no replacement date for existing-environment enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment setting enable disable API PowerShell organization business applications participation. Opened the complete Business Applications in Work IQ default settings article; it says the November 2026 schedule is deferred and to check for updates, without a new date.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Scope: optional coding plugin
claims.claim: The coding plugin is user-opt-in: a developer installs and uses it rather than the separate Work IQ rollout enabling it automatically.
claims.quote:
Install the plugin for your coding agent.
After installation, ask your coding agent: Connect to my Dataverse environment.

claims.claim: Work IQ environment participation is configured at Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote:
Select Manage, and select the environment.
Select Settings > Product > Features.
Locate Work IQ.
Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: An automation operation for the Work IQ environment-participation setting is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ participation API Power Platform CLI organization table settings; Work IQ environment setting enable disable API PowerShell; organization intelligence. Read manage-participation, default-settings and organization-table search excerpts; no mapped Work IQ setting operation found.

claims.claim: The tenant control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings.
In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the tenant Business Applications data availability control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot Graph API PowerShell; graph/api Copilot Dataverse settings. Read default-settings and manage-ai-experience-access and search results; none documents an automation operation for this tenant audience control.

claims.claim: Allowed MCP clients are configured at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > client > Is Enabled.
claims.quote:
Select Manage > Environments.
Under Settings, select Product > Features.
Select Advanced Settings.
Open the client record you want.
On the MCP client record, set Is Enabled to Yes.

claims.claim: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients(<allowedmcpclientid>) updates an allowed MCP client record.
claims.quote:
Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients
Primary key: allowedmcpclientid
Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.claim: The allowed-client PATCH body uses isenabled, with false disabling and true enabling the client.
claims.quote:
isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled
Default options
1 | Yes
0 | No

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP server can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Select Agents > Tools.
Select Work IQ MCP.
Review its current availability.
To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the Work IQ MCP server's tenant Block control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP Block Graph API tool management; graph Work IQ MCP block update. Read manage-ai-experience-access and Graph/tool-management search excerpts; no API mapped to this server's Block control found. Generic API Management controls do not establish that mapping.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; controls[4].api; controls[4].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: No separate coding-agent Dataverse plugin access switch is documented beyond the underlying identity permissions and tool-specific controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse plugin coding agents enable disable admin switch licensing price. Read agents-plugin/, coding-agents and security-governance. No separate coding-plugin UI/API switch found; the Cowork installation control concerns a different host.

claims.claim: Dataverse environment access and security roles govern what the signed-in developer's plugin can do.
claims.quote: An agent can't exceed the permissions of the signed-in identity. If that identity lacks a required privilege, the operation fails.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant cascade setting stops sharing between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse even when an app is configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.claim: The Copilot Chat cascade is not a universal block on directly authenticated plugin tools.
claims.quote: Other tools used by the plugin, such as the Dataverse SDK for Python and Power Platform CLI, authenticate directly and aren't subject to these MCP-specific controls. Their requests still require Dataverse authorization.

claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP Block control covers the entire server and is separate from the Copilot audience control.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access.

claims.claim: The printed allowed-client REST call changes one client record rather than the server-wide setting.
claims.quote:
An MCP client that is allowed to talk to MCP endpoint
Primary key: allowedmcpclientid
isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled

claims.claim: Role-based skill access requires both Skill Sharing Role and the security role with which the skill is shared.
claims.quote: Security role access requires users to have two roles. An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.
